MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

L13·N279unmasked layer
This neuron sits mostly in negative territory: it rises to its (weak) maximum on ordinary sentence punctuation — mainly commas and periods, plus occasional mid-sentence function words ("with", "stake") — inside flowing natural prose or tag lists, and is strongly suppressed at boundaries inside structured/technical boilerplate (code namespaces like `::`, product-name fragments like "Bo|atLIFE", `)` in legislative records, newline before a repeated dataset title).

L13·N6011unmasked layer

L13·N11121unmasked layer
Rather than a single surface form, this neuron gives diffuse mid-level activation across opinionated, debunking/critical commentary (false beliefs, hype, pretense, misleading claims), peaking on the content word that carries the accusation — e.g. "pretending", "machine" in "hype machine", "phrase" in "catchphrase", the suffix "-ably" in "unjustifiably", or "the" in "believe is the cause"; very similar rhetorical contexts can instead drive it strongly negative ("unquestion(ably)", "overexaggerated", "getting more movie roles?").
